controller_determination.rule: The controller must be the legal entity that actually determines the purposes and essential means of the AI4WORK needs-analysis research; website branding, consulting role, hosting-account ownership and project-applicant status must not be treated as interchangeable by assumption.
evidence_required: current MySMIS applicant/leader identity and mandate for the needs analysis
documented decision identifying which legal entity determines the research purpose and essential means
documented role of the eucons.ro site/operator in questionnaire delivery and analysis
documented role of the hosting-account holder and Claus Web in the processing chain
Article 28-compatible instructions/terms for every processor or subprocessor role

candidate_legal_basis: GDPR Article 6(1)(f) legitimate interests — candidate only after controller determination and signoff

purpose_test.interest: produce a documented, evidence-based needs analysis concerning digital/AI skills and training needs for the AI4WORK STEP project concept and associated funding application

necessity_test.why_primary_research_is_needed: secondary official evidence can establish structural context but cannot alone evidence respondent-level perceived skills gaps, barriers, use patterns and employer-reported capability needs
less_intrusive_design: no names, contact details, CNP, exact address or employer identity
controlled broad region/age/status/occupation or sector categories only
no analytical free-text fields; respondent answers are constrained to predefined categories, ratings, booleans and matrices
no login, files, cookies, fingerprinting or cross-site tracking
no CRM or commercial analytics integration
separate optional follow-up contact mechanism with no response linkage

balancing_test.reasonable_expectations: participants are shown a pre-form research notice and make a voluntary positive choice to submit a needs-analysis questionnaire; the data are not reused for enrolment, marketing or individual decisions
balancing_test.data_nature: low-granularity professional/demographic categories plus controlled questionnaire answers; direct identifiers, free-text responses and Article 9/10 data are forbidden
balancing_test.impact: low under the intended design; principal residual re-identification risk comes from combinations of low-granularity categories/small cells and from infrastructure logs, not from respondent free text
balancing_test.power_imbalance: employed and unemployed adults may have contextual vulnerability; participation must not be requested by an employer in a way that creates pressure and refusal must have no disadvantage
safeguards: voluntary participation and clear no-disadvantage language
right-to-object channel disclosed in Article 13 notice
no raw respondent-level response use with external LLM/AI providers
no automated decisions or respondent scoring
logging minimisation and no IP/user-agent in analytical exports
balancing_test.provisional_outcome: A LEGITIMATE-INTEREST OUTCOME MAY ONLY BE SIGNED AFTER CONTROLLER DETERMINATION AND WHILE ALL SAFEGUARDS REMAIN TRUE

fail_closed_conditions: controller legal entity and role are not documented
privacy contact and right-to-object process are not operational for the determined controller
Article 13 notice is not delivered before data submission
processor/subprocessor or transfer review is not completed
server logs make responses routinely linkable to identifiable IP/device data without a documented necessity/retention control
free-text response fields are introduced without a renewed minimisation and privacy assessment
direct identifiers, special-category data, CRM linkage, marketing reuse or individual decision-making are introduced
raw respondent-level records are sent to an external AI/LLM processor without a new legal/privacy assessment
